The Court made the following:
UJUDGMENTU: (per Hon'ble The Acting Chief Justice Sri Manoj Kumar Tiwari)
1. Since common questions of law and facts are involved
in all these writ petitions, therefore, they are being heard
and decided together. However, for the sake of brevity Writ
Petition (S/B) No. 349 of 2021, shall be the leading case.
2. Petitioner in WPSB No. 349 of 2021 is serving as
Associate Professor in department of Rasa Shashtra and
Bhaishjaya Kalpana, in Gurukul Campus of Uttarakhand
Ayurveda University, Dehradun. According to him, he was
given ad-hoc appointment as Lecturer in Government
Ayurvedic College, Gurukul Kangri, Haridwar on 24.10.2008
and he was regularly appointed on the said post on the
recommendation of Uttarakhand Public Services Commission
w.e.f. 19.02.2010. According to him, he was promoted as
Associate Professor on 29.12.2014 and is holding said
position ever since then. The order of promotion dated
29.12.2014 is on record, as Annexure-2 to the writ petition.
3. Perusal of promotion order dated 29.12.2014 reveals
that personal promotion under Career Advancement Scheme
was given to petitioner which is different from vacancy based
2

2024:UHC:9406-DB
promotion as is given in other government departments.
Career Advancement Scheme was introduced by University
Grants Commission, as teachers serving in the Universities
were facing acute stagnation for want of promotional
avenue, as all teaching positions, including Associate
Professor and Professor were required to be filled by open
selection alone.
4. Under Career Advancement Scheme, a person directly
appointed as Lecturer/Assistant Professor, can be given
designation and pay-scale admissible for the next higher post
of Associate Professor, after putting in certain years of
service, however it is a personal promotion and upon
retirement, resignation or death of the teacher, who was
given personal promotion, the post on which he was
appointed by open selection, will fall vacant and not the post
which he was holding before his death, resignation or
retirement. Thus, a teacher promoted under Career
Advancement Scheme, carries the induction level post, on
which he was appointed by open selection, with him upon
promotion to a higher position.
5. In this writ petition, petitioner contends that he is
serving as Associate Professor w.e.f 29.12.2014, therefore,
he is eligible for regular promotion to the post of Professor,
but Uttarakhand Ayurveda University has not concluded
promotion exercise initiated on 14.02.2020, in which,
petitioner also participated.
6. Grievance raised by petitioner is that in the
advertisement dated 09.07.2021, issued by Uttarakhand
Ayurveda University, not a single post of Professor Rasa
3

2024:UHC:9406-DB
Shashtra was reserved for Scheduled Caste category
candidates, which is in violation of reservation policy.
7. In the counter affidavit, filed by Dr. Rajesh Kumar,
Associate Professor on behalf of respondent No. 1, it is
stated that in the department of RAS SHASHTRA, one post of
Professor is held by a person appointed by open selection
and Professor is promoted from the post of Associate
Professor under Career Advancement Scheme and the
remaining vacancies shall be filled as per norms.
8. In para 5 of counter affidavit, it is stated that process of
personal promotion under Career Advancement Scheme is
proposed and it will be initiated as per Clause 35 and 36(i) of
the University Byelaws-2015.
9. Learned counsel for petitioner submitted that since post
of Professor is lying vacant, therefore, University is under a
duty to constitute departmental promotion which shall
consider claim of the petitioner for promotion as Professor.
Petitioner has relied upon Uttarakhand Ayush (Ayurvedic
College Teachers) Service Rules, 2011 in support of his claim
for promotion. The said Service Rules, however, are
applicable only to teachers serving in Government Ayurvedic
Colleges, while petitioner is serving in Uttarakhand Ayurveda
University, which is an autonomous body.
10. Learned counsel for petitioner submitted that there are
as many as 43 sanctioned posts of Professor in different
departments of Uttarakhand Ayurveda University, however,
persons belonging to scheduled caste category are not
adequately represented as per reservation policy applicable
4

2024:UHC:9406-DB
in the State. He further submitted that University issued an
advertisement on 11.02.2020, whereby applications were
invited for appointment against 26 posts of Professor in the
University, out of which 8 posts were reserved for candidates
belonging to scheduled caste category.
11. He submitted that aforesaid advertisement was
cancelled and another advertisement was issued on
09.07.2021 by which, only 16 vacancies on the post of
Professor were notified, out of which 5 were reserved for
scheduled caste candidates. Thus, according to petitioner,
reservation policy is violated by the University by reserving
less number of posts of Professor in the University than
required, thus the impugned advertisement dated
09.07.2021, is liable to be set aside.
12. However, when a pointed query was put to learned
counsel for petitioner as regards the total posts presently
occupied by persons belonging to scheduled caste category,
in the cadre of Professor, learned counsel for petitioner could
not give any reply. He also could not answer our query
regarding the quota, if any, fixed for promotion from
Associate Professor to the post of Professor. The writ petition
is also silent on these aspects. In the absence of these
necessary particulars, the contention raised by petitioner
regarding breach of reservation of policy, cannot be
examined.
13. Petitioner has also sought a direction to consider his
claim for promotion. According to him, in the promotion
exercise, initiated on 14.02.2020, he was called for
interview. Learned counsel for University, however, submits
5

2024:UHC:9406-DB
that petitioner is a teacher serving in University and vacancy
based promotion is not available to teachers of University
and they are only given personal promotion under Career
Advancement Scheme. He submits that under Career
Advancement Scheme, a teacher, if recommended for
promotion in his first attempt is given personal promotion
from the date he became eligible for such promotion and no
loss is suffered by the concerned teacher on account of delay
in completing promotion exercise.
14. Learned counsel for the University has referred to
Clause 36 of the Uttarakhand Ayurveda University Statute,
2015, which provides that academic qualification for
appointment to teaching positions would be such as is
prescribed by University Grants Commission / Central
Council for Indian Medicine / Central Homeopathic council
/State Government, and he submits that the Rules framed by
these agencies have been adopted by Uttarakhand Ayurved
University. He further submits that the Career Advancement
Scheme floated by University Grants Commission, as
adopted by State of Uttarakhand, is applicable in the matter
of promotion in the University.
15. In the absence of any statutory provision creating right
of vacancy based promotion in favour of petitioner, no
direction can be issued to University to promote petitioner to
the post of Professor.
16. As submitted by learned counsel for University,
petitioner can be considered only for personal promotion
under Career Advancement Scheme introduced by University
Grants Commission, therefore, his claim will be considered
6

2024:UHC:9406-DB
as per the said Scheme as and when he becomes due for
such promotion.
17. The Writ Petition is, accordingly, disposed of in
aforesaid terms.
